question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{3}{s}+\frac{2}{s-3},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{3}{s}-\frac{1}{s-3}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
$x(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,+\,\,$ {{field-2}} $\,\,{e}^{3t}$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{3}{s}+\frac{2}{s-3}\} \\  & =3{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}+2{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\  & =3\cdot 1+2{e}^{3\cdot t} \\  & =3+2{e}^{3t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{3}{s}-\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\  & =3{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}-{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\  & =3\cdot 1-{e}^{3\cdot t} \\  & =3-{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3+2{e}^{3t} \\ 3-{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}
$$
